q: How will CCTS carbon credit certificates trade on India's power exchanges?
title: How CCTS certificates trade
short: Under BEE's October 2026 draft procedure, buyers and sellers bid on CERC-registered power exchanges in a closed, double-sided auction with one uniform clearing price per session. The registry checks sellers hold the certificates first. Bilateral deals, even within a corporate group, are not allowed.
audience: Obligated plants, traders and voluntary buyers

sections.h: How a session works in the draft
ol: Registered entities place sell or buy bids on one or more power exchanges.
After the window closes, each exchange sends sell bids to the Grid-India registry.
The registry checks each seller's total bids across exchanges against the certificates in its account.
The exchange discovers the market clearing price and volume by closed double-sided uniform price auction.
The registry debits sellers and credits buyers, and exchanges publish results and demand-supply curves.

ul: Entities registered on the ICM portal are registered with the registry automatically.
Issued certificates are credited to a plant's account after it pays a crediting fee set by CERC.
A seller whose bids exceed its holdings is treated as a defaulter for that session; more than three defaults in a quarter bars it for six months.
The underlying CERC regulations on purchase and sale of certificates were issued on 27 February 2026.

senseible: Senseible does not trade certificates. It keeps the plant-level energy records behind the emissions figure.
